items.title: Elden Ring’s A24 adaptation is in the can — and a crew member said so before the post disappeared
items.summary: A prop artist by the name of Sean Schofield put a photo on Instagram, described the gig as the "Dream job to end all dream jobs," and then the post was gone.
items.content:
A prop artist by the name of Sean Schofield put a photo on Instagram, described the gig as the “Dream job to end all dream jobs,” and then the post was gone. His profile went with it.

That’s how we know A24’s Elden Ring movie has officially finished production.

What Schofield shared was an image of a thank-you note signed by director Alex Garland and producers Allon Reich, Matthew Penry-Davey, Peter Rice, Andrew Macdonald and Charlie Reed. The note rested on an Elden Ring-branded backpack, beside a keychain shaped like a clapboard — standard wrap-gift fare from a studio to its crew.

“Dear cast and crew, thank you for your incredibly hard work on Elden Ring. Your skill, dedication, and all-round professionalism were integral in bringing this unique project to life. We wish you a well-earned rest. Thank you and very best wishes, Alex, Allon, Matthew, Peter, Andrew and Charlie,” the message reads.

It’s the caption that rewards a second read. “Six solid months of blood, sweat and tears making the coolest stuff ever, working alongside the best of the best. Can’t share anything else for a very long time, but I couldn’t be more proud of what we did,” Schofield wrote.

Then, mid-writeup, the post disappeared. The profile flipped to private as well. Somewhere, a phone call got made.

Cameras started rolling in Spring 2026. The release date is set for March 3, 2028.

Run the numbers and you get more than a year of post-production, which makes sense. Putting George R. R. Martin and Miyazaki’s world on screen will lean hard on the visual effects team, and rendering the Lands Between won’t come cheap.

Set photos surfaced online in April, shortly after production began. They depicted the execution of the Dung Eater and of Queen Marika, played by Emma Laird.

That points strongly toward a prequel. The events appear to be set before the game, during the period of history preceding The Shattering that broke the Lands Between apart.

Labels stuck on boxes in the background of those images hinted at the Royal Capital of Leyndell appearing, with Stormveil Castle floating as another candidate. Props glimpsed on set imply the Academy of Raya Lucaria is folded in somewhere.

Nick Offerman, Havana Rose Liu, Jonathan Pryce, Peter Serafinowicz and Cailee Spaeny make up the cast. The budget has been reported at more than $100 million.

Coming from a studio built on arthouse economics, that figure is the loudest thing about the entire production — louder even than a deleted Instagram post.

And Schofield can’t discuss it for a very long time. He said as much himself, just before he couldn’t say anything at all.

items.title: Long-Awaited Epic Fantasy Adaptation Finally Crosses Major Milestone
items.summary: The most expensive film its studio has ever made is done shooting after six months, and there is still a very long wait ahead.
items.content:
A character holding a small knife wearing armor looking at The Lands Between in Elden Ring FromSoftware By Caroline Preece Published Jul 31, 2026, 7:14 AM EDT Caroline Preece has more than 15 years of experience writing entertainment content. Her work for outlets including Den of Geek, Backstage, Tom’s Guide, CultBox, and Starburst prioritizes sharp analysis and reader-first reporting with a particular interest in the ways storytelling, audience behavior, and digital culture drive modern entertainment trends.

Video game adaptations have gone from industry punchline to reliable business in the space of about five years, though the riskiest of them are still the ones built out of worlds fans have already spent hundreds of hours living inside. One such project has been shooting in near-total secrecy since the spring, on a budget its studio has never come close to before, under a director who reportedly finished the source material seven times over before he ever went near a pitch meeting.

That stretch is now over. Elden Ring , Alex Garland's live-action take on FromSoftware's 2022 dark fantasy, has wrapped after roughly six months of production. A24 and Bandai Namco confirmed in April that the adaptation would open on March 3, 2028, shot for IMAX, with a cast led by Kit Connor, Cailee Spaeny, Ben Whishaw, and Nick Offerman, and a budget north of $100 million that makes it comfortably the most expensive film A24 has ever mounted.

Melania holding her arm in a fight with Radahn in concept art for Elden Ring Bandai Namco Entertainment Inc. Word of the wrap came from the crew rather than the studio. Prop maker Sean Schofield posted a photo on Instagram of a wrap gift and a thank-you note signed by Garland and producers Allon Reich, Peter Rice, Andrew Macdonald, Matthew Penry-Davey, and Charlie Reed, calling the job the "dream job to end all dream jobs." The post has since come down, and Schofield's account has been set to private, which is maybe what you would expect from a production that has kept this tight a grip on its own material. A24 has not commented publicly on the wrap.

Garland's claim on this one has always been unusually personal for a studio adaptation. He is a genuine FromSoftware obsessive, and rather than wait to be offered the job, he wrote the script on spec and took it to Hidetaka Miyazaki himself, along with dozens of pages of visual reference. George R.R. Martin, who built the backstory the game rests on , is producing.

FromSoftware Wrapping principal photography in July for a March 2028 release leaves something like 19 months of post, which is a long runway even by the standards of effects-heavy fantasy. Given what the Lands Between actually requires on screen, from Erdtree vistas to boss designs fans can recite from memory, that timeline doesn't read as troubled.

What fans have to go on until then is thin. Set footage that leaked in the spring showed a faithful recreation of the Church of Marika, and the cast Garland has assembled points to a story reaching well beyond the Tarnished. A24 held its casting reveal for 11 months after Garland was confirmed, so a first look is unlikely to arrive in a hurry.

items.summary: A now-deleted post from a prop maker who worked on the film tells us shooting has wrapped.
items.content:

Subscribe to our newsletter here! * Required field E-mail * Name * --> HQ initPlayerScript('801813'); Well over a year before it releases in theatres in March 2028, the Elden Ring movie has wrapped production. A crew member who worked on the film has shown off their wrap gift for the movie, indicating that Alex Garland's A24 fantasy epic is going to have plenty of time ahead for post production, likely due to all the effects needed to bring the Lands Between to life.

As reported by Polygon , prop maker Sean Schofield shared a picture of his wrap gift on Instagram . It came with a card from Garland as well as other key members of the crew on set, thanking everyone for their hard work. "Dream job to end all dream jobs. 6 solid months of blood, sweat and tears making the coolest stuff ever, working alongside the best of the best. Can't share anything else for a very long time, but I couldn't be more proud of what we did," Schofield wrote.

The post on Instagram has since been deleted, but kitconnor.italia (gotta love fan accounts) caught the image and shared it before it was deleted. It's possible that Schofield was asked to take his post down to not leak details about the film, but already word has spread that the Elden Ring movie is that much closer to completion.

Depending on how many effects and how long a film needs to be in post-production, it's not unheard of for a shoot to end well over a year before a movie's release. A24 is staking a lot on Elden Ring being a success, and to get that done it needs to ensure everything looks just right.

The Elden Ring movie releases on the 3rd of March, 2028.

Alex Garland's adaptation of the FromSoftware hit is locked for theaters on March 3, 2028, here is what we know so far. News By GBest - Jul 30, 2026 09:07 PM EST Filed Under: Dark Souls A24's long-awaited Elden Ring movie has reached a major production milestone. Principal photography on the live-action adaptation of FromSoftware's landmark 2022 open-world game is essentially complete, according to a crew member who worked on the project. The film remains on track for a theatrical release on March 3, 2028 .

Prop maker Sean Schofield, whose previous credits include The Witcher and The Rings of Power , shared the news on Instagram on Thursday. He posted a photo of what appears to be a wrap gift alongside a thank-you note signed by director Alex Garland and producers Allon Reich, Matthew Penry-Davey, Peter Rice, Andrew Macdonald, and Charlie Reed. Schofield described the experience in glowing terms.

"Dream job to end all dream jobs," he wrote. "6 solid months of blood, sweat and tears making the coolest stuff ever, working alongside the best of the best. Can't share anything else for a very long time, but I couldn't be more proud of what we did."

Schofield's post marks the first concrete confirmation from someone inside the production that filming has largely concluded. The project has been shooting for roughly four months of principal photography, though Schofield's own involvement stretched across six months of prop and practical work. That timeline lines up with the scale expected for a FromSoftware adaptation. Elden Ring is not a straightforward narrative. Its story is fragmented, its world is vast, and its visual language is dense with unique architecture, armor, and creatures that demand careful translation to live action.

Over the past several months, set photos and paparazzi shots have offered occasional glimpses of that translation in progress. Images circulating online have shown costumed performers in roles that appear to match Queen Marika, the Dung Eater, and Sorcerer Rogier. Backgrounds and partial sets have also surfaced that strongly evoke Stormveil Castle and the misty expanses of Liurnia of the Lakes. None of these images have been officially confirmed by A24 or Bandai Namco , but the level of detail visible in the leaked material suggests the production has prioritized practical sets and costumes wherever possible before the inevitable heavy visual effects pass begins.

That visual effects work is the next major phase. With principal photography nearly finished, the film moves fully into post-production. The nearly two-year gap between the end of shooting and the March 3, 2028 release date is a clear signal of how much digital heavy lifting remains. Creating a convincing version of the Lands Between on screen will require extensive creature work, environmental extensions, magic effects, and large-scale battle sequences. A24 has not yet commented on the production status, so we will have to wait and see what they say.

The project itself was first announced in May 2025 by A24 and Bandai Namco . Alex Garland signed on to write and direct. Garland is best known for cerebral, high-concept films such as Ex Machina , Annihilation , and Civil War . He is also an open and enthusiastic FromSoftware fan. Reports indicate he has finished Elden Ring roughly seven times and has similar experience with the Dark Souls series. That level of personal investment reportedly played a role in securing the rights. Garland is said to have written a 160-page script on speculation, complete with an additional 40 pages of visual reference material, before approaching FromSoftware president Hidetaka Miyazaki. The package was enough to convince the studio to move forward with the adaptation.

Garland's track record with adapted material is solid. He previously wrote the screenplays for Never Let Me Go , Annihilation , and Dredd , each based on existing source works. Those projects suggest he is comfortable working within established worlds while still imposing a distinct authorial voice. Whether that approach will satisfy players who treat Elden Ring's lore as sacred text remains to be seen, but the combination of Garland's personal investment and Miyazaki's reported approval at least raises the odds of a respectful adaptation rather than a purely commercial one.

The cast assembled so far is notably varied. Confirmed names include Kit Connor, Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, Ruby Cruz, Nick Offerman, John Hodgkinson, Jefferson Hall, Emma Laird, and Peter Serafinowicz. Specific roles have not been officially locked down in public statements, though online speculation has already begun matching certain actors to major figures from the game. The presence of performers with both prestige and genre experience is consistent with A24's usual approach of blending arthouse credibility with broader commercial potential.

Adapting Elden Ring was never going to be a simple proposition. The game deliberately withholds clean narrative answers. Its story is told through item descriptions, environmental storytelling, and cryptic dialogue rather than traditional cutscenes or exposition dumps. Translating that approach into a two-hour-plus film requires structural choices that will inevitably leave some players feeling something essential has been lost. At the same time, the game's visual and atmospheric strengths give a filmmaker with Garland's sensibility a rich foundation to work from. The Lands Between is already cinematic in its scale and mood. The challenge is preserving that tone while delivering a coherent dramatic experience for audiences who may never have touched a controller.

The long post-production window also reflects the current reality of large-scale fantasy filmmaking. Even with practical sets and costumes, the volume of digital work required for a project of this scope is enormous. FromSoftware's games are defined by their meticulous craftsmanship and distinctive art direction. Matching that standard on screen will take time, and the 2028 release date gives the production room to do so without the usual compressed theatrical deadlines that often compromise effects-heavy films.

For now, the most tangible progress is the near-completion of filming. A crew member with direct experience on the project has confirmed the wrap, shared photographic evidence of the thank-you notes, and described the work in strongly positive terms. The cast list is public. The release date is locked. And the director is someone who has repeatedly demonstrated both technical skill and a genuine appreciation for the source material.

What remains is the long, quiet phase of post-production. Editing, visual effects, sound design, and scoring will determine whether the finished film captures the strange, mournful grandeur of Elden Ring or simply borrows its most recognizable imagery. Until more official information emerges from A24 , the clearest signal is the one that just arrived from the set itself: principal photography is done, and the long wait for the Lands Between on the big screen has officially begun.

What are your thoughts on the report? Are you excited for an Elden Ring movie? Will you buy tickets to watch it at midnight? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

items.title: Elden Ring player discovers secret item hidden inside a statue after four years
items.summary: Player discovers one of the most important items in Elden Ring
items.content:
After four years, an Elden Ring player discovers a secret

Four years after its release, an Elden Ring player discovers a hidden item that just so happens to be one of the most important items in the game.

For good reason, FromSoftware is considered to be one of the best video game developers in the industry, after treating us to such bangers as Dark Souls , Bloodborne and Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice , to name a few, and the topic of today’s discussion, 2022’s Elden Ring .

Elden Ring is amazing for multiple reasons. Its world is enticing, yet it offers a gruelling sense of adventure of the unknown, challenging but fun combat, stunning yet haunting visuals, and so many secrets that players all over the world will still be making discoveries today.

“Found this while exploring Stormhill. Does it have any significance? Is it supposed to do something?” asked Redditor Choppedman6969. To no surprise whatsoever, fellow Redditors were keen to provide some answers.

“You can’t attack it, but other things can,” hinted JeebaRock. “Ask the troll, he’ll tell you,” added Junior_Seesaw1819.

Basically, the fellow Reddit users were hinting that the player isn't able to smash the object on the screen. But if you have a giant troll to chase you (one can be seen in the background of the image shared by the Redditor), you can trick it into hitting the statue and smashing it to bits. Then the player will be able to acquire a hidden item that was inside it.

Sure, this hidden item will be known by many players, but Elden Ring is welcoming new players all the time. What’s old news to us is the exact opposite for others.

Inside the statue is a Smithing Stone. This is one of the most important materials in the game, because it’s used to increase the power of your weapons, which can give you a big boost when combating enemies. It’s probably the main reason players grind the game when they’re initially struggling to defeat a boss.

READ MORE: Elden Ring: The Convergence Is A Free DLC-Sized Release That Adds Hours Of New Content

FromSoftware is known for its gruelling action RPGs, where constant death is a lesson on how to improve in the game, not only with your combat skills, but also mental resilience, and Elden Ring is no exception.

However, Elden Ring is one of the most accessible games from the famed developer, because it’s easier to get a friend, random or an NPC Spirit Ash to join you to take on a badass boss.

The map of the Lands Between is open from the get-go, so you could explore and grind XP till your heart's content, and it has generously placed save points (Sites of Grace) scattered throughout the map, and more. It’s these kinds of life features that made first-time FromSoftware gamers welcome to Elden Ring .

Elden Ring is out now on PC, PlayStation and Xbox. It’s also coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on August 28, 2026.

items.title: 'The Coolest Stuff Ever' — Elden Ring Movie Prop Artist Reveals Filming Has Officially Wrapped
items.summary: Production has officially wrapped for A24’s Elden Ring movie, as revealed in a now-deleted Instagram post from prop artist Sean Schofield.
items.content:
Production has officially wrapped for A24’s Elden Ring movie , as revealed in a now-deleted Instagram post from prop artist Sean Schofield.

Schofield shared a photo of a special message celebrating the project from director Alex Garland, as well as producers Allon Reich, Matthew Penry-Davey, Peter Rice, Andrew Macdonald, and Charlie Reed.

“Dear cast and crew, thank you for your incredibly hard work on Elden Ring. Your skill, dedication, and all-round professionalism were integral in bringing this unique project to life. We wish you a well-earned rest. Thank you and very best wishes, Alex, Allon, Matthew, Peter, Andrew and Charlie,” the message reads.

The photo shows the small message sitting on top of an Elden Ring-branded backpack and a keychain with a clapboard, which were likely given as gifts to crew working on the film.

"Dream job to end all dream jobs," Schofield wrote in the post’s caption. "Six solid months of blood, sweat and tears making the coolest stuff ever, working alongside the best of the best. Can’t share anything else for a very long time, but I couldn’t be more proud of what we did."

It seems that he may have shared this particular bit of news too early, as the post was taken down right in the middle of writing this article. You can't even find his profile right now, suggesting he made it private.

Production for the video game adaptation started in Spring 2026, with and is scheduled to release on March 3, 2028. That leaves over one year for post-production, which we can imagine will be quite demanding on the special effects team, given the not-insignificant amount of CGI that will likely be needed to bring George R. R. Martin and Miyazaki’s vision to life.

This is the latest news to surface from the film after a series of set photos leaked online in April, shortly after production began, showing the execution of the Dung Eater and Queen Marika, played by Emma Laird. As noted by IGN’s own Wesley Yin-Poole, this hints that the events in the film will likely take place before the game, exploring what life was like before the Lands Between were wracked by The Shattering.

Other information gleaned from the photos strongly suggested that the Royal Capital city of Leyndell will make an appearance in the movie, as could Stormveil Castle, thanks to labels plastered atop boxes on set. Props were also spotted that hint the Academy of Raya Lucaria will somehow get worked in.

A24’s Elden Ring cast includes stars like Nick Offerman, Havana Rose Liu, Jonathan Pryce, Peter Serafinowicz, Cailee Spaeny, with a reported budget of more than $100 million . The arthouse studio is sparing no expense for this flick, and we can't wait to see how they tackle the Lands Between come March 2028.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

items.title: I'm Just Not Into Souls Games, I'm Being Tested Enough As It Is
items.summary: I am taking the opportunity this week to get something off my chest, something I haven’t been able (or willing) to share so publicly before: I hate Souls games. All of them. Even the ones that don’t have Souls in their name, because they still count. 🤝This is
items.content:
I am taking the opportunity this week to get something off my chest, something I haven’t been able (or willing) to share so publicly before: I hate Souls games. All of them. Even the ones that don’t have Souls in their name, because they still count.

Whether it’s Demon’s Souls or its sequel, Sekiro or Bloodborne or Elden Ring , if there’s enough Miyazaki and unforgiving combat in it to warrant being called a Souls Game, get it out of my face. I don’t want anything to do with it. I would rather punch myself unconscious than subject myself to its trials.

I understand this can be a sacrilegious thing to say as a games writer. It is generally held that these games are beloved by all, respected by consumer and critic alike, some of the all-time greats of the medium. I literally cannot think of anyone else I have been able to share my disdain with in professional (or even personal!) circles; everyone else is always “oh this boss was so hard” this and “I died 117 times before getting past this bit, it was AMAZING” that.

I am a middle-aged man whose life currently consists of a succession of ordeals. I have seen my career blown up twice through no fault of my own . I am trying to pay off a mortgage with declining income amid an inflationary crisis. To do this, I am working three jobs, one of which involves begging strangers for money on a weekly basis, and which for three 16-hour days of the week I have to fit around another job. I have two teenage kids.

The very last thing I want to do when I sit down at the end of a very long day is to suffer more trials. I do not want to have to act fast, to memorise patterns, to beat my head against a boss 99 times in the pursuit of fun. I need my personal time to relax , and these games are the opposite of relaxing! And I certainly don’t feel the need to prove anything to myself by beating a "hard" video game either, I am not 12 years old, I know where my strengths (and weaknesses!) are by now, both in gaming and as a person. I can see the appeal there for others, and will never try to tell you not to enjoy these games, but for me and my needs and my tastes, the premise of a game built around repeated failure and precise timing is torture.

I find this really interesting, though, because as someone who has played hundreds of video games over the last 20 years I can’t think of another major series where I am even remotely as repulsed as I am by Souls games. I love Yakuza , and it’s got the same menu obsession and (in older titles at least) a more forgiving version of its punishing melee combat. I’ve always found something to get me through a AAA shooter , I like driving cars, I’ve played too many FIFA games and even in the handful of Nintendo franchises I’ve bounced off ( Metroid ) there’s something to admire. I have even, gasp, found space in my heart to fall in love with a Hideo Kojima game . Fast or slow, easy or hard, I have loved games (or found something to love within them) across the genre and difficulty spectrum.

But Souls games? It’s like they’re precision-engineered to bounce right off me, in every way humanly possible. I hate everything , from the art design (yuck) to the combat to the relentless concentration required to do anything to the way that so many people are so slavishly in love with something I detest, a big “we love Souls ” club that seems to include everyone I know except me and…

Ah. As I lean further back into the therapist’s couch I've conjured in my mind while writing this, maybe there's something in that. A lot of the games I truly love, the ones with little guys and taking turns , are often relatively niche pursuits, never getting anywhere near the kind of popular critical mass Souls games enjoy, something everyone I know can talk about online or at a party. Maybe I don’t just hate the game, I hate the players as well, because everyone always seems to be having so much fun beating things and talking to friends about it and falling in love with a very particular kind of game and I’m left out because I just don’t feel the same way. Bah humbug, etc, and all that entails.

Oh well! Fuck it. I still don’t like the games, I’m never going to pretend I do just so I can be part of some online discourse. If that means living the rest of my days as a Souls hater, forever on the outside looking in (on the internet), then so be it!

It's Hater Week here on Aftermath . This week we’re letting the hate flow through us by examining what it means to be a hater (and… a lover?), venting about some of our biggest pet peeves in games and life, and giving others a space to do the same.

items.title: Mistfall Hunter looks like legally distinct Elden Ring but with a faster paced, extraction spin
items.content:
Image credit: Bellring Games News by Oisin Kuhnke Contributor Published on July 28, 2026 15 comments Follow Mistfall Hunter On its surface, aesthetically Mistfall Hunter certainly looks like a game where if you were doomscrolling and briefly saw a gif of it in action, you'd be forgiven for thinking it's from Elden Ring . The game certainly apes FromSoftware's dark fantasy, selectively colourful vibe, but it is offering up something different under the hood at least, as rather than your dime a dozen soulslike , it's opted for the slightly trendier extraction approach.

The general brutality of Soulsian games can still be found here, the game's trailer puts plenty of bits of dodge rolling, parrying, a range of classes to play around with from those that lean towards melee and others that have a focus on magic, and various subsets of builds to be found within those. Pace-wise, combat seems to be a bit faster than the usual FromSoft affair, it's not necessarily as slow and methodical.

The key thing here is that extraction loop, in which you find yourself in a land where you must hunt for something called Gyldenblood and hunt for some relics, attempting to get out safely while you do so. It's a PvPvE kind of situation, so while of course you may find yourself up against some nasty NPC beasties, other folks might waltz up and finish you off after a tough battle. Best to keep yourself on your toes. It's also playable in solo or trios, so perhaps round up some friends if you're one who typically avoids PvP in Souls games.

It also sounds like there's plans to change things up from season to season. As explained over on the game's Steam page, "The battlefield beneath the Gyldenmist constantly mutates, unleashing new classes, forbidden arcana, uncharted zones, and ancient relics to keep the hunt fresh and fiercely competitive." Certainly sounds like it's taking a similar approach to other live service extraction games, I'm just curious to see whether the soulslike audience will enjoy this particular flavour of challenge.

Mistfall Hunter is also out soon! Very soon in fact, slated for release July 30th. You can wishlist it on Steam here .

items.title: 7 Soulslike Games That Rival Elden Ring
items.summary: FromSoftware's Elden Ring might be the best soulslike game ever, but these titles stand alongside it.
items.content:
FromSoftware's Elden Ring might be the best soulslike game ever, but these titles stand alongside it.

Originally published by Game Rant Add Us On follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Elden Ring is the biggest and most popular soulslike game of all time, and many would argue it stands unrivaled as the genre's crowning achievement . While few projects match the scope, depth, and addictiveness of FromSoftware's masterpiece, exceptions not only exist, but some are even better than Elden Ring in certain ways. They might offer superior combat, bosses, atmosphere, or world structure.

The Lands Between is a special place that continues to serve as home for countless players, and that won't change anytime soon. However, those same folks might want to take a trip to another soulslike realm that could very well become their favorite place away from home, and not all of these games are from FromSoftware.

Bloodborne is now over a decade old, but aside from FPS lock, the game hasn't aged a day. From the moment players step into the world, it is very clear they are in for something special, as everything from the towering structures to the eerie skybox creates a sense of darkness and intrigue that never goes away until the end credits finally roll.

While previous games had their own parry mechanics, here guns become the player's tool for deflection, setting up some incredibly visceral sequences in which they quickly dispatch and destroy anything and anyone that dares to take a swing at them. The standout, though, will always be the world and the stories within it, both taking heavy influence from Lovecraftian fiction to deliver a horrific yet enticing experience that will have players begging on their knees for more.

Team Ninja certainly took a liking to the soulslike format, essentially spending the last decade exploring the genre. While the FromSoftware inspiration is plain for all to see, Team Ninja quickly established its own niche that combines soulslike exploration with more aggressive-than-usual combat akin to the developer's earlier Ninja Gaiden games. Nioh 3 comes arguably the closest to being an Elden Ring proxy due to its open-world design, and it is fantastic; however, Nioh 2 remains the franchise's high point.

If I had to pick one way to describe Nioh 2 , it would be "a lot." Like Elden Ring , the game gives you all the tools and systems you could possibly need to take on the many challenges that await over the 50-hour campaign, and that goes beyond the variety of melee and ranged weapon types that greatly influence your playstyle.

Players can switch between three stances at any given time, all of which are viable and useful. They need to master the Burst Counter, a counter that utilizes the player's Yokai power to interrupt enemies. Then there are dozens of Soul Cores, which summon Yokai for a single attack. So much to learn, and it's so much fun.

It is pretty fair to say that when Sekiro exploded onto the scene, the entire soulslike genre was shaken down to its very core. Gone were the days of slow, methodical exploration, and in their place was fast, unforgiving combat that relied solely on reaction speed and muscle memory in a way no other game in the space had even come close to.

Mechanically, it remains at the top of the genre, demonstrating a level of precision and satisfaction that many have tried to replicate, but very few have succeeded. Then there are the boss fights, each posing a different kind of challenge to the player, and all requiring a huge amount of knowledge and patience in order to take them down. Elden Ring might have the scale, but Sekiro checks every other box, with the most important being the gameplay and the actual mechanics that players will come to learn and master over time.

Hollow Knight doesn't look like the traditional third-person soulslike many people associate the genre with, yet the gameplay and the design of the game quickly reveal that it more than fits the criteria. The way the game unfolds feels so organic and natural, something that Elden Ring definitely excels at, but here, the environments are far more claustrophobic and intimate, making the player feel one with the world throughout their long and perilous journey.

The goodness doesn't stop there, as players will find themselves tested to their absolute mechanical limits, with their platforming mechanics and their combat prowess being pushed far further than they may have expected. By the time players have scoured the map for caterpillars and conquered just about every foe in sight, they may think the adventure is coming to an end, but that's exactly when the game throws a curveball and introduces a brand-new cavern of secrets for them to explore and fall in love with all over again.

items.title: Is Elden Ring the best of the Souls series?
items.summary: Is Elden Ring the best Soulslike game ever made? Explore how FromSoftware reinvented the genre with open-world freedom, epic boss fights, and unmatched player choice.
items.content:
For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games.

For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games and inspired players of all ages.

Let’s take a look at how ELDEN RING has elevated and perfected the original Souls series formula and explore if ELDEN RING could be the best of the entire Souls series.

The majority of the games were designed by Hidetaka Miyazaki to give players the experience of exploring dark and majestic fantasy worlds full of danger.

There’s also a strong focus on difficulty, world structure, boss fights, and player builds.

The difficulty of the Souls series stems from their combat design. They emphasize deliberate attack and evasion in response to enemy movement, which tends to be quick, fierce, and punishing for players who find themselves out of position at the wrong moment. Players need to carefully observe and learn their foes’ patterns, then react to exploit certain specific attack openings without leaving themselves open as well.

This type of careful, evasive gameplay mimics the danger and strategy of real hand-to-hand combat and the high stakes keeps the tension and excitement rising in each fight. It’s not as simple as playing out a power fantasy where enemies easily fall to repeated mindless button mashing. For most players, this difficulty means that the feeling of mastering Souls series combat is a rush of pure accomplishment.

In the earlier Souls series games , levels are massive, interconnected linear paths. These paths often have several branching paths that reward exploration and puzzle solving, but are limited in terms of true open field exploration, as it’s necessary to follow a specific set order of levels, usually connected by a hub area where players can regroup, level up and open new paths, to progress throughout the game.

In the best Souls series games , carefully studying the environment and enemy behavior can lead to hidden areas or items, a particular strength of the Dark Souls series, and many players consider level design that rewards careful exploration to be a critical feature of Dark Souls-like games .

Throughout the Souls series , boss battles are powerful climatic moments that put a player’s abilities to the test. In the Dark Souls series , specifically, from the Asylum Demon to Slave Knight Gael , the Dark Souls bosses are encounters that inspire fear, awe, pity, and wonder.

Bosses also act as progression gates that require a certain level of fluency with the game’s combat system before the player can continue to explore. Once a player reaches a boss gate, they must either muster the skill to defeat that boss, or continue to practice and grind on earlier enemies.

Unlike the average enemy that players must face in a limited area not much wider than a typical hallway, bosses are frequently found in massive arenas. Bosses in the Souls series also tend to have enhanced abilities that require the player to adapt to attacks that cover huge areas or have extended reach. This ferocity and enlarged battlefield gives the designers space to create exciting, multi-phase duels that are unforgettably intense.

These boss fights also act as a check on the player’s build. No matter which weapons or elements a player prefers, massive and powerful bosses require adaptation.

Experienced players understand how each type of stat affects their damage output and they use all of the gear at their disposal to create a move set that fits their style and is powerful enough to take down bosses.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack

items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
